title: Intel (INTC) CEO says quantum computing will become mainstream within three to five years
source_used: Reuters text as published by The Economic Times (Newsquawk page read first: one-line headline plus unsourced market commentary)
key_facts: Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan spoke on Monday (12 Oct 2026) at a panel organised by the lender DBS.
He said quantum computing could become mainstream in the next three to five years.
He added that software will play a role in driving the efficient use of some of the infrastructure that will be required.
The same Reuters report is mostly about Chinese AI models: Tan said their token costs have been lower and adoption 'very fast', and their performance 'good enough'.
Tan named DeepSeek, Kimi and GLM, and said he is a strong believer in open source as the best way to drive efficiency.
quote_evidence: He added that quantum computing could become mainstream in the next three to five years and that software will play a role in driving the efficient use of some of the infrastructure that will be required.
At a panel organised by lender DBS on Monday, Tan said the performances of Chinese models, such as DeepSeek, Kimi and GLM, are "good enough".
why_it_matters_hint: One major chipmaker chief executive gives a public three-to-five-year horizon for quantum computing; the report gives no Intel product or spending behind it.
notes: The Newsquawk page carries only the headline (which says 'will') plus unsourced market commentary; the Reuters text says 'could', so the pool headline overstates. The Economic Times printed the Reuters report; the original Reuters link was not found, so the Economic Times page is the link. Newsquawk commentary (optimistic end of range, no disclosed Intel quantum revenue) is its own opinion and was not used as fact.
